# HL7® Rust

> HL7®, and FHIR® are the registered trademarks of Health Level Seven International and their use of these trademarks does not constitute an endorsement by HL7.

Parse, navigate, validate, modify, and render Health Level Seven (HL7)
messages in Rust. A Cargo workspace of fourteen small, mostly
dependency-free crates: HL7 v2 (releases 2.1-2.9) with three parsing
modes and a command-line tool, a foundation for HL7 v3, format
conversion between ER7 (pipe-delimited), the official v2.xml, and JSON,
transports (MLLP, SOAP), and tooling to build a vendor dictionary from a
site's own XSDs. This is an independent project, not affiliated with or
endorsed by Health Level Seven International.

## Start here

- [Documentation](https://hl7-rust.github.io/docs/): install it, run it, and learn the vocabulary the rest of this site assumes
- [Install](https://hl7-rust.github.io/docs/install/): every crate, every feature flag, and the command-line tools
- [hl7-skill/SKILL.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/hl7-skill/SKILL.md): HL7 concepts, terminology, and ideas, with worked examples — read this first to learn the vocabulary
- [Quick start](https://hl7-rust.github.io/docs/quickstart/): a real message parsed, queried, edited, and answered, in about five minutes
- [Concepts](https://hl7-rust.github.io/docs/concepts/): the full vocabulary this project and this file assume

## Crates

- [hl7](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7/): umbrella crate — `hl7::v2` and `hl7::v3` today, room for `hl7::fhir`
- [hl7-2](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2/): HL7 v2 itself — parse, navigate, validate, modify, render; also the `hl7-v2` command-line tool
- [hl7-3](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-3/): HL7 v3 — RIM backbone classes, coded values, the three-level message envelope; a foundation, not a full implementation
- [hl7-2-derive](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-derive/): `#[derive(FromHl7)]` / `#[derive(ToHl7)]`, behind `hl7-2`'s `derive` feature
- [hl7-3-derive](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-3-derive/): `#[derive(FromElement)]`, behind `hl7-3`'s `derive` feature
- [hl7-2-mllp](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-mllp/): HL7 v2 framed on a TCP stream (MLLP)
- [hl7-2-soap](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-soap/): HL7 v2 carried in a SOAP envelope over HTTP
- [hl7-3-soap](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-3-soap/): HL7 v3 carried in a SOAP envelope over HTTP — v3's own historically dominant transport
- [hl7-2-from-er7-into-json](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-from-er7-into-json/): ER7 -> typed JSON
- [hl7-2-from-json-into-er7](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-from-json-into-er7/): typed JSON -> ER7
- [hl7-2-from-er7-into-xml](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-from-er7-into-xml/): ER7 -> official v2.xml XML
- [hl7-2-from-xml-into-er7](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-from-xml-into-er7/): v2.xml XML -> ER7
- [hl7-2-from-xsd-into-json-dictionary](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-from-xsd-into-json-dictionary/): HL7 v2.xml XSDs -> the JSON dictionary `hl7-2` reads
- [hl7-2-xml-lite-helper](https://hl7-rust.github.io/crates/hl7-2-xml-lite-helper/): minimal XML reader shared by the v2.xml crates and `hl7-3`

## Specifications (normative)

- [spec/conformance](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/spec/conformance/index.md): what "supports HL7 v2 releases 2.1-2.9" means, exactly — segments, types, and structures by name
- [spec/phi](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/spec/phi/index.md): what these crates do with protected health information, and where a value can escape into a log
- [spec/benchmark](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/spec/benchmark/index.md): how the published performance figures are measured
- [spec/rust-msrv-n-minus-2](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/spec/rust-msrv-n-minus-2/index.md): the minimum supported Rust version policy
- [Specifications index](https://hl7-rust.github.io/spec/): every crate's own `spec/index.md`, the single source of truth for that crate's behavior — where anything else disagrees with it, the spec wins

## Agent skills

- [hl7-skill/SKILL.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/hl7-skill/SKILL.md): HL7 concepts, terminology, and ideas for end users, with examples from this repo
- [hl7-rust-maintainer-skill/SKILL.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/hl7-rust-maintainer-skill/SKILL.md): implementation-level conventions for changing this workspace's own code, specs, and docs

## Governance and policy

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): how to file a report, what a good pull request needs, and how to help without writing code
- [MAINTAINERS.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md): who maintains this, the bus factor, and what happens if the maintainer is unavailable
- [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md): who decides, what is in scope, and how to become a maintainer
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability and what counts as one
- [Patient data](https://hl7-rust.github.io/docs/patient-data/): plain-language answers about patient data, for a privacy officer or reviewer
- [TRADEMARKS.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/TRADEMARKS.md): the consolidated HL7®/FHIR® trademark position
- [AI_STATEMENT.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/AI_STATEMENT.md): how AI tools are used to build this, and who is accountable
- [LICENSE.md](https://github.com/hl7-rust/hl7-rust/blob/main/LICENSE.md): MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0-only OR GPL-3.0-only
